title: IVR Voice Gateway wire contract v1
description: Text control/event messages exchanged over the /v1/media WebSocket alongside raw PCM16LE binary audio frames. Audio is never JSON: binary frames are 8 kHz mono 16-bit little-endian, 20 ms (160 samples, 320 bytes).

Start.description: client -> server. First message after the socket opens. A client may stamp its own seq/at, as the reference SDK does; the server does not rely on them.

hint.description: Context from the IVR (caller id, menu choice, account, character preference).

Started.description: server -> client. The gateway accepted the call.

final.description: false while the utterance is still being refined.

Reply.description: server -> client. A sentence the agent will speak; audio frames follow.

Dtmf.description: A keypad digit pressed during the call. Travels both ways: the client sends it without seq/at, and the gateway echoes it back as an event carrying both.

sensitive.description: When true the digit group is redacted from the transcript and never sent to the model.

Digits.description: server -> client. A completed read_digits group. A sensitive group carries count and hash only: the digits themselves are never written to the event log nor sent to the model.

label.description: What was collected, echoed from the read_digits action.

count.description: How many digits the caller entered.

digits.description: The digits entered. Absent when redacted is true.

redacted.description: True when the group was collected as sensitive.

hash.description: Keyed correlation token (truncated HMAC-SHA256) standing in for a redacted group, so the same entry can be recognised across calls without storing it. Present only when redacted is true.

Action.description: server -> client. The agent acts on the call. The adapter executes it (AMI/ARI/dialplan).

Escalation.description: server -> client. The agent is handing the call to a human. The handoff packet carries everything the human needs to continue the conversation.

identity.description: Who the caller is (name, account, phone number).

intent.description: Why they called, in the agent's words.

entities.description: Named values extracted during the call (account_number, order_id, etc.). Values are strings.

actions_taken.description: What the agent already did or offered.

sentiment.description: Caller's emotional state (calm, frustrated, angry, etc.).

summary.description: Brief natural-language summary for the human agent.

Stop.description: client -> server. Caller hung up or the IVR is ending the leg. A client may stamp its own seq/at, as the reference SDK does.

Ended.description: server -> client. The gateway closed the call and flushed the event log.

Error.description: server -> client. A protocol or provider error.
